title: Unreliable Shared Calendar — Even with Premium
text:
Unreliable Shared Calendar — Even with Premium

I pay for a TimeTree Premium subscription, but I have experienced recurring problems with the shared calendar. The person I share my calendar with suddenly sees a completely blank calendar, even though all the appointments are still visible on my end. This has happened more than once.

A shared calendar needs to be reliable. When appointments unexpectedly disappear from the other person’s view, it creates confusion and makes coordinating schedules difficult. As a paying customer, I expect this essential feature to work consistently. I need TimeTree to address this issue and provide a lasting solution.

Another issue I have experienced is that when the two people sharing a calendar are in different time zones—for example, when one person is in another country—the app does not properly synchronize appointment times between them. This creates additional confusion and makes it difficult to coordinate schedules reliably.

title: Decent calendar hindered by cost
text:
With the amount of shared calendars on the App Store it’s difficult to distinguish yourself apart from the rest. TimeTree has a deep set of options with thoughtful features to make planning and organizing relatively easy. While some options are intuitive, others are a bit convoluted and unnecessarily complicated with too many button clicks to achieve a simple task. 

The biggest flaw though is the pricing: $4.50 per month or $45 a year. Again, there are dozens of other shared calendar apps that, more or less, do the same thing with the same features for less money. Why would I pay PER PERSON for a subscription that I will be sharing with one or more people? This is just price gouging for no justifiable reason. No family plans is essentially a deal breaker when other apps offer this kind of subscription and are more inexpensive. 

TimeTree wants to stand out from the pack but they are not doing themselves any favors with their pricing. They are more focused on overcomplicating their app—MORE FEATURES!— while overvaluing their product. People who are paying for this app are getting ripped off and haven’t done their due diligence to look into other, more affordable options.

title: Needs to step up the tech game
text: I’m a long time fan of TimeTree but recently I’ve run into issues using AI with it. First, none of the AI models that I know of can talk to or edit TimeTree which is normal for Google Calendar and a must have for those of us using AI ALas a personal assistant. Also, TimeTree can’t be exported to Google Calendar despite having seamless importing. With the increasing use of agentic AI, this app desperately needs to be more friendly to these features. If it doesn’t soon I’ll be switching back to Google Calendar which can do the same basic things I ask of TimeTree but for free and fully usable with AI.
